parameters.name: document_type
parameters.description: Document type path token (e.g. POLICY_CERTIFICATE, or HEALTH_CARD/{dependant_id})

400.description: Invalid or missing dependant_id (HEALTH_CARD requires it)

403.description: Not owner or dashboard user

AccountDetails.description:
Tagged JSONB blob persisted into `accounts.account_details`. Mirrors
`accounts.account_type` — types that carry extra metadata (e.g.
`SAVINGS` → IFSC) embed it; the rest are unit variants. Bank account
numbers / PBA UUIDs live in `accounts.external_account_id`.

AccountType.description: Type of financial or health account.

AddressDetails.description:
Structured address details for user profiles and insurance documents.

All fields except `line2` are **required** — serde rejects a structured address
missing any of `line1`, `city`, `state`, `country`, or `pincode` (presence is
enforced by the type, not by a value-level validator). A fully free-text
address is captured via [`AddressDetailsOuter::Raw`] instead.

line2.description: Apartment, suite, unit, or building (line 2). Optional.

oneOf.description: Original free text plus the structured fields derived from it.

AddressDetailsOuter.description:
A user-submitted address as captured: either the structured form, a single
free-text string, or both (the original text plus whatever was structured
from it). `#[serde(untagged)]` keeps the wire shape natural — a bare object
or a bare string — so existing structured clients are unaffected.

`raw` is `Secret` because a free-text address is PII (it embeds the same
data masked elsewhere as `line1` / `pincode`).

AmountType.description: Represents a monetary amount with its associated currency

AnsweredQuestion.description:
A question paired with the user's boolean answer.

Used both as:
- the request-side payload at policy create / preview time, and
- the persisted snapshot on `insurance_policies.questionnaire`.

`question` text must match the benefit's wording exactly — server rejects
stale or mismatched questionnaires.

AppConfigResponse.description:
Feature flags consumed by the mobile app to enable/disable UI affordances.

A verbatim passthrough of every key in the dedicated app-facing
Superposition workspace (`[superposition].app_workspace_id`). The backend
does not interpret these values — adding a flag is purely a Superposition
change (admin UI + app fallback TOML), no backend redeploy. The app owns
the default for any key absent from the map.

BankDetails.description: Origin-bank details required to open a purpose-bound account at PBA.

account_number.description: Origin bank account number. Sensitive — never logged in plaintext.

ifsc_code.description: IFSC code of the origin bank branch (11 chars, e.g. "HDFC0000001").

BenefitEntityStatus.description: Generic, coarsened lifecycle of a benefit_entity — a benefit-agnostic projection of each benefit's own status (mirrors ExternalMandateStatus -> MandateStatus), so goal/mandate reactions never see insurance/consultation vocabulary. CREATED = just recorded (insurance Pending, consultation Initiated). VERIFICATION = the member has reached the clinic and is being verified (insurance Verification); it is the entitlement's echo of the front desk, not the queue's own status. APPROVED = insurance Approved. ACTIVE = live (insurance Issued/renewal, consultation Active). REJECTED = never went active (insurance Rejected). COMPLETED = went active then ended (insurance Expired/Reissuance, consultation Completed/Closed). FAILED = a technical/operational failure distinct from a rejection (consultation Failed). REJECTED, COMPLETED and FAILED are terminal but drive different reactions.

BenefitProviderKind.description: Which provider backs a benefit. Drives consultation provider dispatch. Currently hardcoded to Narayana at the call site; will move onto the benefit_provider record later. Serde-only for now — not a standalone DB column, so no diesel_enum.

BenefitType.description: Kind of benefit offered by a provider. Stored as TEXT — deliberately not a PostgreSQL enum, so adding a kind needs no migration.

ClinicQueueStatus.description: Where a member sits in the clinic front-desk workflow, for any benefit type. CREATED = admitted to the queue, not yet arrived. IN_PROGRESS = arrived at the clinic and being seen. COMPLETED = terminal. Deliberately not insurance vocabulary — the queue spans every benefit type, so it does not borrow PolicyStatus's `verification`. Distinct from BenefitEntityStatus, which tracks the entitlement rather than the visit: one is written by the clinic operator, the other by the benefit pipeline.

ConsultationStatus.description: Consultation lifecycle status. INITIATED = row inserted, upstream thread not yet created (transient or stuck). ACTIVE = upstream thread open (mirrors chatStatusCategory OPEN). COMPLETED = doctor marked done (mirrors DONE). CLOSED = archived (mirrors CLOSED). FAILED = upstream create_thread errored after our INSERT; not visible to FE.

oneOf.description: The customer's phone number (PII → masked in logs).

value.description: The customer's phone number (PII → masked in logs).

oneOf.description: The platform's own identifier for the customer.

value.description: The platform's own identifier for the customer.

ContributorReference.description:
A typed reference to the contributing customer, adjacently tagged on the wire
as `{ "type": "PHONE" | "CUSTOMER_ID", "value": "…" }`. Passthrough context —
carried in the contributor token; the backend does not resolve the customer
from it (yet).

Currency.description:
ISO 4217 three-letter currency codes.

Currently INR only; add variants as the product expands.

DeductionSchedule.description: When a `PlanAdditionalCharge` on an insurance plan variant is deducted. A dedicated enum rather than reusing `MandateFrequency` because it must express fixed timing anchors — `START_OF_POLICY`, `END_OF_YEAR`, `END_OF_POLICY` — that a recurring debit cadence has no vocabulary for. Serde-only: serialized inside the `benefit_details` JSONB, not a standalone DB column, so no diesel_enum.

DependantNominee.description: A nominee who is an existing dependant in the system.

Duration.description:
A length of time expressed in a single unit.

Wire format: externally-tagged union — single-key object whose key is the
unit name (`days` / `months` / `years`) and whose value is the integer
count. Example: `{"months": 12}` or `{"years": 1}`.

EventLogSchema.description: Which schema's `event_log` audit table to read: one table, never a union. Defaults to `PUBLIC`.

ExternalNominee.description: A nominee who is an external person not registered as a dependant.

GetBalanceResponse.description:
Response shape mirrors PBA's `GetBalanceOutput` byte-for-byte (snake_case
field names, no extra wrapping). All monetary amounts are in the smallest
currency unit (e.g. paise for INR).

platform_id.description: One of the user's ACTIVE platforms, as listed by `GET /platforms`.

GoalCategory.description:
Closed category set for a `category:`-purpose goal. Stored as the snake_case
segment inside the [`GoalPurpose`] URN (e.g. `category:healthcare`), never as
its own column. The canonical set is business-owned; extend here when product
confirms new categories.

GoalPurpose.description:
What a goal is for. The DB stores this as a single `purpose` VARCHAR(64) column
URN-encoded as `<kind>:<payload>`:

- `category:<GoalCategory>` — a closed category (e.g. `category:healthcare`).
- `specific:<benefit_entity_id>` — one benefit instance; the payload is the
  `benefit_entities.entity_id` (validated at create, no DB FK — like `Source`).

Every kind carries a payload, so a bare kind is always a parse error.

Every entry point (JSON `Deserialize`, diesel `FromSql`, `FromStr`)
re-validates so corrupt rows fail loudly.

GoalStatus.description: Goal lifecycle — terminal-vs-live only. ACTIVE from creation; CLOSED = ended at its natural end (term elapsed, e.g. policy expiry); CANCELLED = never went live (e.g. the funding policy was rejected). Whether a goal is *running right now* is answered by its term (start_time..end_time), not by this status — a goal is ACTIVE even when its term starts in the future. Target-met and spend outcomes are computed, not stored on status.

HolderKind.description:
Discriminator for [`Holder`] variants. Used at the wire boundary for
split-field admin query params (`?holder_kind=user&holder_id=...`).
Not stored as a DB column — the DB has only the URN-encoded `holder`
column.

InsurancePolicyMetadata.description: Auxiliary metadata for an insurance policy.

provider_metadata.description:
Free-form provider data captured during admin bulk update
(e.g. from insurance provider reconciliation CSVs). Any columns not
mapped to the structured update fields are stored here verbatim.

MandateExecutionStatus.description: Internal lifecycle status of a mandate-execution (autopay) firing, independent of the linked order's `external_status` (Juspay vocabulary). Inserted as `Initiated` when the Kronos firing is claimed, advances to `Pending` once the charge is dispatched, and lands on `Success`/`Failed` from the `/orders` reconciliation. Distinct from `OrderStatus` so the firing's vocabulary can diverge from the payment's. See `From<&ExternalOrderStatus>` for the provider-status mapping.

MandateFrequency.description: Debit frequency for a mandate. Mirrors Juspay's wire enum.

MandateStatus.description: Internal mandate lifecycle status — coarse-grained view derived from the raw Juspay status string. Starts at INITIATED the moment a registration row is created (before/while the Juspay session is opened) and advances to PENDING/CREATED/etc. as Juspay reports progress. CREATED is where a Juspay-approved registration lands; there is no separate ACTIVE, which only ever duplicated it.

MinorUnit.description: This Unit struct represents MinorUnit in which core amount works

allOf.description: The nominee is an existing dependant.

oneOf.description: The nominee is an existing dependant.

allOf.description: The nominee is an external person not registered as a dependant.

oneOf.description: The nominee is an external person not registered as a dependant.

NomineeDetails.description:
Nominee for an insurance policy — either a registered dependant or an
external person whose details are captured inline.

Occupation.description: Occupation of a user. Stored as TEXT — deliberately not a PostgreSQL enum, so adding a value needs no migration.

OrderMedium.description: How an order's money moves — the settlement rail, orthogonal to `source` (whose money). PAYMENT = a user-initiated Juspay collect (manual self top-up); MANDATE = a debit against the user's registered mandate (scheduled autopay, and tips); SPONSOR = an internal PBA transfer from the sponsor's account. Autopay-self and tip share MANDATE and split on `source`; the credit doorbell keys the goal leg off `source`, not `medium`.

OrderMetadata.description:
Typed wrapper over the `orders.metadata` jsonb column, also returned
verbatim as `OrderResponse.metadata`.

`payment_method_type` / `payment_method` are filled later from Juspay's
order-status response.

The Juspay `/session` blob is deliberately absent. The frontend needs it
once, to open the payment page, so the create response carries it straight
from the session call as `OrderResponse.payload`; nothing reads it back
afterwards, and storing it only parked a large provider blob per order.

OrderStatus.description:
Local lifecycle status of an order, independent of the provider's `external_status` (Juspay vocabulary). Inserted as `Initiated` before the Juspay `/session` call so the row is always traceable, advances to `Pending` once the session is created, and lands on `Success`/`Failed` from the first terminal poll. See `From<&ExternalOrderStatus>` for the provider-status mapping.

Three states are tip-only and sit outside that arc. `Expressed` precedes `Initiated`: a contributor has declared a tip, but the upstream has not finished so nothing is collectable yet. `Declined` is terminal and no provider status can produce it — the upstream finished without the tip being collected, which is distinct from `Failed` (a collection was attempted and refused) and from `ExternalOrderStatus::JuspayDeclined` (a declined *payment*). `RecoveryFailed` is the one that matters operationally: the tip WAS collected upstream and already sits in the beneficiary's platform earnings, but the mandate debit that recovers it onto the goal failed. Unlike `Failed`, where no money moved anywhere, this leaves a real-world imbalance — the money exists, we could not retrieve it — so it is a distinct state a follow-up can act on rather than a generic failure. Backed by a Postgres enum: adding a variant needs an `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` migration alongside the Smithy edit.

PlatformUserStatus.description: User-platform membership lifecycle status. `INACTIVE` is the soft-delete state; `(user_id, platform_id)` is the primary key, so a revoked membership is flipped back to `ACTIVE` in place on the next login.

Question.description: A single yes/no question definition (benefit side, no answer attached).

Relationship.description: Relationship of a dependant to the primary user.

required.description:
`false` still advertises the field to the client as worth collecting — it
just does not block. On a collection it governs whether the collection
may be **empty**, independently of the nested rules below.

requirements.description:
Requirements every member of this collection must satisfy — the same
shape, one level down. Only meaningful on a collection-valued field
(today just DEPENDENTS); rejected anywhere else.

RequirementField.description:
Identity of a requirement.

The variant set is **closed**. Unlike `plan_code` or a provider-defined
questionnaire key (both free-form because the provider owns that
vocabulary), these name our own columns, so a typo must not silently disable
a check. The resolvers in `aarokya::utils::benefit_requirements` match
exhaustively, which means adding a variant fails compilation until it has a
way to be resolved.

Salutation.description: Title or honorific for a person.

SenderRole.description: Who sent a consultation message. Classified server-side from the upstream sender metadata; UNKNOWN is the forward-compat fallback when no signal is available.

Sort.description:
Sort specification for list endpoints. Read the field names as
"sort **on** `<column>` **by** `<direction>`".

oneOf.description:
Field / column to sort on. `None` means "use the endpoint default"
(`created_at`).

SortOn.description:
Field-name half of a [`Sort`]. Closed enum of the sortable columns
across the app — when a new sortable column is needed, add a variant
here. Storage layers exhaustively match on this so adding a variant
forces a compile error at every call site that needs to translate it.

Not every table carries every column: an append-only ledger has no
`last_modified_at`, so its `list()` maps that variant back to the
default rather than growing a column it must not have.

SponsorKind.description: Kind of sponsor — individual person or organisation.

SystemEventKind.description: Kind of provider-emitted system event surfaced inside a consultation message. OTHER is the forward-compat fallback when the adapter sees an upstream kind it does not yet know — keeps the message stream parseable instead of failing the page.

TimeRange.description:
A half-open time range, with a mandatory start and an optional end.
Designed to be embedded in list/filter query params via `#[serde(flatten)]`.

`Deserialize` runs [`TimeRange::validate`] as part of deserialization, so
callers never receive a [`TimeRange`] that violates `start_time <= end_time`.

end_time.description: Inclusive end time; defaults to "now" when omitted.

TipType.description: Which tip rail a contributor token is for. INDIRECT = tipped on the platform's own surface and recovered through the goal's mandate (`MANDATE` medium); DIRECT = paid to our merchant (`PAYMENT` medium), no mandate. Serde-only: carried in the token claim, never stored, since the order's `medium` already records the rail.

TransactionSummary.description:
Mirrors PBA's `TransactionSummary` field-for-field. Open-ended string
fields (`type`, `status`, `pool`, `direction`) are passed through as
strings rather than re-typing as enums — keeps the wire format identical
even if PBA adds a new variant we haven't seen yet.

account_kind.description: `pb` or `normal`. Optional because older PBA responses may omit it.

correlation_id.description: PBA correlation id linking paired ledger entries (e.g. transfer debit ↔ credit).

pool.description: Pool segment for PB-account transactions; absent on normal-account.

access_token.description: A freshly minted app token, carrying the updated identity claims. Present only when the caller is the app user themselves; absent for dashboard / service callers, which hold no app token to refresh.

UserId.description:
A validated 12-digit numeric user identifier.

Every external entry point validates:
- JSON `Deserialize` runs [`UserId::parse`] (outer whitespace trimmed,
  length and digit-only enforced) via `#[serde(try_from = "String")]`.
- DB `FromSql` runs [`UserId::parse`] on every row read.

`Display` / `Deref<Target = str>` / `AsRef<str>` / `Into<String>` are
derived via `derive_more` — the inner `String` is pass-through for
every read-only borrow, display, and move-out.

WalletTxnStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of the wallet-side transaction attached to an order.

Wallet-agnostic — today PBA, tomorrow any other wallet integration.
The lifecycle has five observable states:

- `Initiated` — order row inserted; no wallet call has been made yet. Set
  at row create-time. Single-phase (interactive add-money) advances
  straight to `Success`; two-phase (mandate-autopay) advances to `Pending`.
- `Pending(deposit_id)` — two-phase Phase 1 succeeded: the wallet provider
  accepted the deposit and returned its id, but it is still parked on the
  provider side waiting for an external settlement signal. Carried between
  the Juspay `/txns` ack and the `/orders/{id}=Charged` reconciliation.
- `Success(deposit_id)` — terminal: the deposit has been finalised at
  the wallet provider (Phase 2 confirm, or single-phase commit). The
  provider's id is the single dedup signal for any further status poll.
- `Voided(deposit_id)` — terminal: a parked `Pending` deposit was
  explicitly released back to the source because the originating charge
  reached a terminal failure. The provider's id is preserved for audit.
- `Failed` — terminal: the originating charge failed before any
  wallet-side deposit was held (Phase 1 never ran or itself failed).

Serialized to text as:
- `initiated`                        → `Initiated`
- `pending:<deposit_id>`             → `Pending(deposit_id)`
- `success:<deposit_id>`             → `Success(deposit_id)`
- `voided:<deposit_id>`              → `Voided(deposit_id)`
- `failed`                           → `Failed`

BearerAuth.description: JWT bearer token. App-user tokens are issued by POST /auth/token (the partner backend calls it as its platform service account); admin and dashboard tokens are issued via OIDC login.
